subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
Subject: week one!!

Hi Manjula,
I'm writing this from the office pantry because my desk neighbour is on a call saying things like 'let's circle back on the SLA' and 'can you send me the deck by EOD'. I nodded like I knew. I did not know. I looked up two of them in the bathroom.
On Monday they gave me a laptop and an ID card with my photo on it, and I actually felt like crying, the good kind. I've wanted to work in logistics since that supply-chain elective with you in second year.
But everyone here talks so fast and so sure. In the Tuesday meeting someone asked my opinion and my mind went blank. Since then I keep wondering if HR mixed up two CVs and picked me by mistake.
Is this normal? Did you feel like this?
Missing the canteen,
Devika

qa.q: Where is Devika writing the email from?
qa.a: Devika is writing from the office pantry.

qa.q: What two feelings is Devika holding at the same time in the first week?
qa.a: Devika is thrilled to be hired, almost crying the good kind of tears, and also anxious that the selection was a mistake.

qa.q: What could Devika try in the second week to feel less lost?
qa.a: Devika could keep a small list of unfamiliar terms and ask a friendly colleague or manager to explain a few, instead of looking them up in secret.

qa.q: What would you want to hear if you were Manjula reading this email?
qa.a: I would want to reassure Devika that feeling lost in week one is common, and share my own first-week story so the worry feels less lonely.

grounding: It shows a fresh graduate in a first job, hearing confident colleagues use unfamiliar terms, mixing the thrill of being hired with worry that it was a mistake.

subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
Tanvir, first day, you want to know? Okay. So I walk into the bank's head office, twelfth floor, glass everywhere, and the team lead is already talking about 'basis points' and 'run-rate' and 'the Q3 walk'. Q3 walk! I thought it was a team outing.
Everyone has two screens. Everyone types without looking. One girl, maybe a year older than me, finished a whole model while I was still trying to log in.
And I'm so happy, Tanvir, I am. My name is on the door list. I called Amma from the lift. But at lunch I sat there thinking, Sudha, they interviewed forty people, and they picked you? What if they meant the other Sudha? There were two Sudhas in the final round, I'm not joking.
I laughed about it in the lift. At night it's not so funny.

qa.q: What floor is the bank's head office on?
qa.a: It is on the twelfth floor.

qa.q: What was Sudha thinking at lunch on the first day?
qa.a: Sudha was worried the bank had picked the wrong person, even joking they might have meant the other Sudha 😰

qa.q: What small step could help Sudha settle in?
qa.a: Sudha could ask the team lead or a nearby colleague to explain a few terms like 'the Q3 walk' in the first week, since new joiners are expected to ask.

qa.q: How might Tanvir react to hearing both the excitement and the worry?
qa.a: Tanvir may be happy for Sudha but also notice how real the self-doubt is, and want to remind Sudha that being picked means something.

grounding: It shows a fresh graduate on the first day, surrounded by confident colleagues and jargon, feeling both excitement at being hired and fear it was a mistake.

subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
Kiran's first day at the analytics firm began with rain and a badge that didn't work. By the time security let Kiran in, orientation had started, and the promised laptop was "still in procurement".
So Kiran sat through the team stand-up with only a notebook. Jomon, a senior analyst, was saying things like "the churn cohort's flat, let's rerun attribution against last quarter's baseline," and everyone nodded. Kiran nodded too and wrote down: churn cohort???
At lunch the manager said, "We were really impressed with your interview." Kiran smiled and felt a small, bright thrill, and right behind it a cold thought: they've mixed me up with someone else. Everyone here knows things I've never heard of.
On the wet bus ride home, Kiran kept opening the offer letter on the phone, as if the name on it might change.

qa.q: What did Kiran write down during the stand-up?
qa.a: Churn cohort???

qa.q: What was Kiran feeling when the manager praised the interview?
qa.a: Kiran felt a bright thrill of excitement mixed with anxiety that the company had made a mistake in the selection.

qa.q: What small step could Kiran take on day two?
qa.a: Ask Jomon or the manager for a list of common team terms, instead of nodding along and quietly worrying.

qa.q: How might Jomon see the new hire nodding in the stand-up?
qa.a: Jomon probably doesn't notice the confusion and assumes Kiran is following, since everyone else nodded too.

grounding: On a chaotic first day a new graduate hears unfamiliar jargon, and the thrill of being hired mixes with fear the selection was a mistake.

subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
On Monday Yamini wore the new blue kurta her mother had ironed twice and took the 8:12 fast local to Lower Parel, grinning at her reflection in the train window. A real job. A salary slip with her name on it.
By eleven the grin had gone stiff. Her team at the bank spoke a different language: KYC exceptions, T+1, recon breaks. Leela, at the next desk, cleared a queue of forty cases while explaining a process on the phone and eating an apple. Yamini opened the training manual and read the same page three times.
At lunch she hid in the washroom and texted a friend: "Everyone here is so smart. I think HR picked the wrong CV." Then she added, "But the view from the 14th floor is unreal 😍"
She went back to her desk, opened a blank page in her notebook and titled it: Words I don't know yet.

qa.q: What title did Yamini give the page in her notebook?
qa.a: Words I don't know yet.

qa.q: What does Yamini's text to her friend reveal about her mixed feelings?
qa.a: She feels anxious that HR picked the wrong CV, yet excited and proud about the job and the view.

qa.q: What could help Yamini in her first weeks?
qa.a: Keep her list of unknown words and ask Leela to explain a few each day, instead of hiding in the washroom.

qa.q: How might Leela see the new colleague at the next desk?
qa.a: Leela is probably busy and doesn't realise how intimidating that speed looks, and might happily help if asked 🙂

grounding: A fresh graduate's excitement at her first job mixes with worry that she was hired by mistake as colleagues use unfamiliar terms.

subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage:
"So? How's day one, madam architect?" Reena asked.
"Reena, I'm hiding in the stairwell."
"What? Why?"
"Everyone is so confident. In the morning meeting they kept saying FAR and setbacks and model coordination, and I just nodded like a dashboard doll."
"You studied five years of this!"
"Not like this. A girl who joined last year was arguing with the partner. Arguing! I can't even find the printer."
"But you're happy you got it?"
"Of course! When they gave me my ID card I wanted to take a selfie with it." Himani laughed, then went quiet. "I keep thinking they'll realise they picked the wrong person."
"Himani, they interviewed you three times."
"Maybe they were tired the third time."
"Go back in. Ask someone where the printer is. That's your only task today."
"...Okay. The printer. I can do the printer."

qa.q: Where is Himani hiding?
qa.a: In the stairwell.

qa.q: What does Himani mean by 'they picked the wrong person'?
qa.a: She feels anxious that her selection was a mistake, even while she is excited and proud to have the job.

qa.q: Why is Reena's suggestion about the printer a good one?
qa.a: It turns a huge worry into one small, doable task, getting Himani back to her desk and talking to colleagues.

qa.q: What is it like for Reena on this call?
qa.a: Reena is amused but supportive, trying to calm Himani's panic with reminders and one tiny task.

grounding: A new graduate at her first job is excited yet worried she was chosen by mistake as colleagues use unfamiliar terms.

subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
passage: On my first day at the logistics software company, I wore the new shirt Amma had ironed twice. The office had bean bags and a coffee machine I didn't know how to use. By ten I was in a stand-up meeting where people said "sprint velocity", "blockers" and "push to staging" as if everyone was born knowing them. I nodded. I wrote the words in my notebook to search later. Abhinav, my buddy for the week, asked, "Yogesh, anything blocking you?" I said, "No, all good," though I couldn't even log into the laptop. At lunch I kept thinking, maybe HR mixed up two CVs. Maybe the real Yogesh is sitting at home. Then I'd remember the offer email, and a small, fizzy excitement would come back. I went home both terrified and thrilled.

qa.q: What did Yogesh write in the notebook?
qa.a: The unfamiliar words, to search later.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Yogesh go home with?
qa.a: Yogesh went home both terrified and thrilled, worried the selection was a mistake yet excited about the job.

qa.q: What small step could help Yogesh on day two?
qa.a: Telling Abhinav honestly about the laptop login and asking what one or two of the terms mean.

qa.q: How might Abhinav see Yogesh on day one?
qa.a: Abhinav likely sees a new joiner who says all is good, not knowing Yogesh could not even log in.

grounding: Shows a fresh graduate on day one surrounded by confident colleagues and unfamiliar terms, excited to be hired but worried it was a mistake.
